(3) Vole de demo am sen basi de awtorita de krasitim; hin vole am bevyata yon watumonli ji awtenti tupyoli seleti hu da am okur yon moyli ji egal tupyoli haki, ji yon sirili tupyo or egaljacipul proceso fe huru tupyo.

(3) The will of the people shall be the basis of the authority of government; this will shall be expressed in periodic and genuine elections which shall be by universal and equal suffrage and shall be held by secret vote or by equivalent free voting procedures.

La voluntad del pueblo es la base de la autoridad del poder público; esta voluntad se expresará mediante elecciones auténticas que habrán de celebrarse periódicamente, por sufragio universal e igual y por voto secreto u otro procedimiento equivalente que garantice la libertad del voto.

La volo de la popolo estu la bazo de la aŭtoritato de la registaro; tiu volo estu esprimata per regulaj kaj aŭtentikaj elektoj, kiuj okazu per universala kaj egala balotrajto, kaj per sekreta voĉdono aŭ ekvivalentaj liberaj voĉdonaj proceduroj.

Der Wille des Volkes bildet die Grundlage für die Autorität der öffentlichen Gewalt; dieser Wille muss durch regelmäßige, unverfälschte, allgemeine und gleiche Wahlen mit geheimer Stimmabgabe oder in einem gleichwertigen freien Wahlverfahren zum Ausdruck kommen.

La volonté du peuple est le fondement de l’autorité des pouvoirs publics ; cette volonté doit s’exprimer par des élections honnêtes qui doivent avoir lieu périodiquement, au suffrage universel égal et au vote secret ou suivant une procédure équivalente assurant la liberté du vote.

Воля народа должна быть основой власти правительства; эта воля должна находить себе выражение в периодических и нефальсифицированных выборах, которые должны проводиться при всеобщем и равном избирательном праве путем тайного голосования или же посредством других равнозначных форм, обеспечивающих свободу голосования.
人民的意志是政府权力的基础;这一意志应以定期的和真正的选举予以表现,而选举应依据普遍和平等的投票权,并以不记名投票或相当的自由投票程序进行。

सरकार की सत्ता का आधार जनता की दच्छा होगी । इस इच्छा का प्रकटन समय-समय पर और असली चुनावों द्वारा होगा । ये चुनाव सार्वभौम और समान मताधिकार द्वारा होंगे और गुप्त मतदान द्वारा या किमी अन्य समान स्वतन्त्र मतदान पद्धति से कराये जाएंगे ।
إن إرادة الشعب هي مصدر سلطة الحكومة، ويعبر عن هذه الإرادة بانتخابات نزيهة دورية تجري على أساس الاقتراع السري وعلى قدم المساواة بين الجميع أو حسب أي إجراء مماثل يضمن حرية التصويت.

A vontade do povo será a base da autoridade do governo; esta vontade será expressa em eleições periódicas e legítimas, por sufrágio universal, por voto secreto ou processo equivalente que assegure a liberdade de voto.

Moyte, kom membro de sosyaltim, haki sosyal anjenya ji, yon nasyonli juhudi ji intrenasyonli tonaksyon ji fe dongwi ton organisa ji resurso de moy nasyon, moyte haki pia realgi fe den ekonomili, sosyal ji kulturali haki beharemusi cel tesu sungen ji cel huru evolu fe tesu personya.

Everyone, as a member of society, has the right to social security and is entitled to realization, through national effort and international co-operation and in accordance with the organization and resources of each State, of the economic, social and cultural rights indispensable for his dignity and the free development of his personality.

Toda persona, como miembro de la sociedad, tiene derecho a la seguridad social, y a obtener, mediante el esfuerzo nacional y la cooperación internacional, habida cuenta de la organización y los recursos de cada Estado, la satisfacción de los derechos económicos, sociales y culturales, indispensables a su dignidad y al libre desarrollo de su personalidad.

Ĉiu, kiel membro de la socio, havas rajton je socia sekureco kaj povas postuli la realigon, per naciaj klopodoj kaj internacia kunlaboro, kaj konforme al la organizo kaj disponeblaj rimedoj de ĉiu Ŝtato, de tiuj ekonomiaj, sociaj kaj kulturaj rajtoj, kiuj estas nepre necesaj por lia digno kaj por la libera disvolviĝo de lia personeco.

Jeder hat als Mitglied der Gesellschaft das Recht auf soziale Sicherheit und Anspruch darauf, durch innerstaatliche Maßnahmen und internationale Zusammenarbeit sowie unter Berücksichtigung der Organisation und der Mittel jedes Staates in den Genuss der wirtschaftlichen, sozialen und kulturellen Rechte zu gelangen, die für seine Würde und die freie Entwicklung seiner Persönlichkeit unentbehrlich sind.

Toute personne, en tant que membre de la société, a droit à la sécurité sociale ; elle est fondée à obtenir la satisfaction des droits économiques, sociaux et culturels indispensables à sa dignité et au libre développement de sa personnalité, grâce à l’effort national et à la coopération internationale, compte tenu de l’organisation et des ressources de chaque pays.

Каждый человек, как член общества, имеет право на социальное обеспечение и на осуществление необходимых для поддержания его достоинства и для свободного развития его личности прав в экономической, социальной и культурной областях через посредство национальных усилий и международного сотрудничества и в соответствии со структурой и ресурсами каждого государства.
每个人,作为社会的一员,有权享受社会保障,并有权享受他的个人尊严和人格的自由发展所必需的经济、社会和文化方面各种权利的实现,这种实现是通过国家努力和国际合作并依照各国的组织和资源情况。

(1) Everyone has the right to work, to free choice of employment, to just and favourable conditions of work and to protection against unemployment.
Toda persona tiene derecho al trabajo, a la libre elección de su trabajo, a condiciones equitativas y satisfactorias de trabajo y a la protección contra el desempleo.
Ĉiu havas rajton je laboro, je libera elekto de sia okupo, je justaj kaj favoraj laborkondiĉoj kaj je protekto kontraŭ senlaboreco.
Jeder hat das Recht auf Arbeit, auf freie Berufswahl, auf gerechte und befriedigende Arbeitsbedingungen sowie auf Schutz vor Arbeitslosigkeit.
Toute personne a droit au travail, au libre choix de son travail, à des conditions équitables et satisfaisantes de travail et à la protection contre le chômage.
Каждый человек имеет право на труд, на свободный выбор работы, на справедливые и благоприятные условия труда и на защиту от безработицы.
人人有权工作、自由选择职业、享受公正和合适的工作条件并享受免于失业的保障。

Todo ser humano tem direito ao trabalho, à livre escolha de emprego, a condições justas e favoráveis de trabalho e à proteção contra o desemprego.

Setiap orang berhak atas pekerjaan, berhak dengan bebas memilih pekerjaan, berhak atas syarat-syarat perburuhan yang adil serta baik, dan berhak atas perlindungan dari pengangguran.
Kila mtu ana haki ya kufanya kazi, ya kuchagua kazi aipendayo, ya kuchagua kazi yenye masharti mazuri na ana haki ya kulindwa asikose kazi.
(2) Moyte, nenhar he ban diskrimina, haki egal paya por egal ergo.
(2) Everyone, without any discrimination, has the right to equal pay for equal work.
Toda persona tiene derecho, sin discriminación alguna, a igual salario por trabajo igual.
Ĉiu, sen ia ajn diskriminacio, rajtas ricevi egalan salajron pro egala laboro.
Jeder, ohne Unterschied, hat das Recht auf gleichen Lohn für gleiche Arbeit.
Tous ont droit, sans aucune discrimination, à un salaire égal pour un travail égal.
Каждый человек, без какой-либо дискриминации, имеет право на равную оплату за равный труд.
人人有同工同酬的权利,不受任何歧视。
प्रत्येक व्यक्ति को समान कार्य के लिए बिना किसी भेदभाव के समान मज़दूरी पाने का अधिकार है ।
لكل فرد دون أي تمييز الحق في أجر متساو للعمل.
Todo ser humano, sem qualquer distinção, tem direito a igual remuneração por igual trabalho.
Herkesin, hiçbir fark gözetilmeksizin, eşit iş karşılığında eşit ücrete hakkı vardır.
Setiap orang, tanpa diskriminasi, berhak atas pengupahan yang sama untuk pekerjaan yang sama.
Kila mtu ana haki ya kupata mshahara sawa na wengine wenye kazi ya namna moja bila ubaguzi.
(3) Moyte hu da ergo haki adil ji propul bocan hu da am yakingi, tas seli te ji tesu famil, sonzay laye fe insanli sungen, ji bucundo, fol haja, fal alo resurso fe sosyal gardi.

(3) Everyone who works has the right to just and favourable remuneration ensuring for himself and his family an existence worthy of human dignity, and supplemented, if necessary, by other means of social protection.

Toda persona que trabaja tiene derecho a una remuneración equitativa y satisfactoria, que le asegure, así como a su familia, una existencia conforme a la dignidad humana y que será completada, en caso necesario, por cualesquiera otros medios de protección social.

Ĉiu, kiu laboras, rajtas ricevi justan kaj favoran kompenson, kiu certigu por li mem kaj por lia familio ekziston konforman al homa digno, kaj kiun suplementu, laŭnecese, aliaj rimedoj de socia protekto.

Jeder, der arbeitet, hat das Recht auf gerechte und befriedigende Entlohnung, die ihm und seiner Familie eine der menschlichen Würde entsprechende Existenz sichert, gegebenenfalls ergänzt durch andere soziale Schutzmaßnahmen.

Quiconque travaille a droit à une rémunération équitable et satisfaisante lui assurant ainsi qu’à sa famille une existence conforme à la dignité humaine et complétée, s’il y a lieu, par tous autres moyens de protection sociale.

Каждый работающий имеет право на справедливое и удовлетворительное вознаграждение, обеспечивающее достойное человека существование для него самого и его семьи, и дополняемое, при необходимости, другими средствами социального обеспечения.
每一个工作的人,有权享受公正和合适的报酬,保证使他本人和家属有一个符合人的生活条件,必要时并辅以其他方式的社会保障。

प्रत्येक व्यक्ति को जो काम करता है, अधिकार है कि वह इतनी उचित और अनुकूल मज़दूरी पाए, जिससे वह अपने लिए और अपने परिवार के लिए ऐसी आजीविका का प्रबन्ध कर मके, जो मानवीय गौरव के योग्य हो तथा आवश्यकता होने पर उसकी पूर्ति अन्य प्रकार के सामाजिक संरक्षणों द्वारा हो सके ।
لكل فرد يقوم بعمل الحق في أجر عادل مرض يكفل له ولأسرته عيشة لائقة بكرامة الإنسان تضاف إليه، عند اللزوم، وسائل أخرى للحماية الاجتماعية.

Todo ser humano que trabalha tem direito a uma remuneração justa e satisfatória, que lhe assegure, assim como à sua família, uma existência compatível com a dignidade humana e a que se acrescentarão, se necessário, outros meios de proteção social.
çalışan her kimsenin kendisine ve ailesine insanlık haysiyetine uygun bir yaşayış sağlayan ve gerekirse her türlü sosyal koruma vasıtalarıyla da tamamlanan adil ve elverişli bir ücrete hakkı vardır.

Setiap orang yang melakukan pekerjaan berhak atas pengupahan yang adil dan baik yang menjamin kehidupannya dan keluarganya, suatu kehidupan yang pantas untuk manusia yang bermartabat, dan jika perlu ditambah dengan perlindungan sosial lainnya.

Kila mfanya kazi anayo haki ya kupata mshahara wa kufaa na unaopendeza utakao mwezesha yeye mwenyewe pamoja na jamaa yake kuishi katika hali bora, na ahifadhiwe-ikiwa lazima- maisha yake kwa njia nyingine.
(4) Moyte haki na organisa ji na membrocu in ergoli asosyatim cel na gardi sesu muhimxey.

Jeder hat das Recht, zum Schutz seiner Interessen Gewerkschaften zu bilden und solchen beizutreten.
Toute personne a le droit de fonder avec d’autres des syndicats et de s’affilier à des syndicats pour la défense de ses intérêts.
Каждый человек имеет право создавать профессиональные союзы и входить в профессиональные союзы для защиты своих интересов.
人人有为维护其利益而组织和参加工会的权利。
प्रत्येक व्यक्ति को अपने हितों की रक्षा के लिए श्रमजीवी संघ बनाने और उनमें भाग लेने का अधिकार है ।
لكل شخص الحق في أن ينشأ وينضم إلى نقابات حماية لمصلحته.
Todo ser humano tem direito a organizar sindicatos e a neles ingressar para proteção de seus interesses.
Herkesin menfaatlerinin korunmasi için sendikalar kurmaya ve bunlara katılmaya hakkı vardır.
Setiap orang berhak mendirikan dan memasuki serikat-serikat pekerja untuk melindungi kepentingannya.

Toda persona tiene derecho a un nivel de vida adecuado que le asegure, así como a su familia, la salud y el bienestar, y en especial la alimentación, el vestido, la vivienda, la asistencia médica y los servicios sociales necesarios;
Ĉiu havas rajton je vivnivelo adekvata por la sano kaj bonfarto de si mem kaj de sia familio, inkluzive de nutraĵo, vestaĵoj, loĝejo kaj medicina prizorgo kaj necesaj sociaj servoj,

Jeder hat das Recht auf einen Lebensstandard, der seine und seiner Familie Gesundheit und Wohl gewährleistet, einschließlich Nahrung, Kleidung, Wohnung, ärztlicher Versorgung und notwendiger sozialer Leistungen, sowie das Recht auf Sicherheit im Falle von Arbeitslosigkeit, Krankheit, Invalidität oder Verwitwung, im Alter sowie bei anderweitigem Verlust seiner Unterhaltsmittel durch unverschuldete Umstände.

Toute personne a droit à un niveau de vie suffisant pour assurer sa santé, son bien‐être et ceux de sa famille, notamment pour l’alimentation, l’habillement, le logement, les soins médicaux ainsi que pour les services sociaux nécessaires ; elle a droit à la sécurité en cas de chômage, de maladie, d’invalidité, de veuvage, de vieillesse ou dans les autres cas de perte de ses moyens de subsistance par suite de circonstances indépendantes de sa volonté.

Каждый человек имеет право на такой жизненный уровень, включая пищу, одежду, жилище, медицинский уход и необходимое социальное обслуживание, который необходим для поддержания здоровья и благосостояния его самого и его семьи, и право на обеспечение на случай безработицы, болезни, инвалидности, вдовства, наступления старости или иного случая утраты средств к существованию по не зависящим от него обстоятельствам.
人人有权享受为维持他本人和家属的健康和福利所需的生活水准,包括食物、衣着、住房、医疗和必要的社会服务;在遭到失业、疾病、残废、守寡、衰老或在其他不能控制的情况下丧失谋生能力时,有权享受保障。

प्रत्येक व्यक्ति को ऐसे जीवनस्तर को प्राप्त करने का अधिकार है जो उसे और उसके परिवार के स्वास्थ्य एवं कल्याण के लिए पर्याप्त हो । इसके अन्तर्गत खाना, कपड़ा, मकान, चिकित्सा-सम्बन्धी सुविधाएं और आवश्यक सामाजिक सेवाएं सम्मिलित है । सभी को बेकारी, बीमारी, असमर्थता, वैधव्य, बुढापे या अन्य किसी ऐसी परिस्थिति में आजीविका का साधन न होने पर जो उसके क़ाबू के बाहर हो, सुरक्षा का अधिकार प्राप्त है ।

Tiuj ĉi rajtoj kaj liberecoj estas en neniu okazo efektivigeblaj kontraŭe al la celoj kaj principoj de Unuiĝintaj Nacioj.

Ces droits et libertés ne pourront, en aucun cas, s’exercer contrairement aux buts et aux principes des Nations Unies.
Осуществление этих прав и свобод ни в коем случае не должно противоречить целям и принципам Организации Объединенных Наций.
这些权利和自由的行使,无论在任何情形下均不得违背联合国的宗旨和原则。
इन अधिकारों और स्वतन्त्रताओं का उपयोग किसी प्रकार से भी संयुक्त राष्ट्रों के सिद्धान्तों और उद्देश्यों के विरुद्ध नहीं किया जायगा ।

Nilto in hin deklara am betafasir denpul kom anxi hu he ban nasyon, grupo or person hare he ban haki na rol fe he ban aksyonya or na okurgi he ban fale hu da cele na destrui he banto of haki ji huruya dingyado in hinto.

Nothing in this Declaration may be interpreted as implying for any State, group or person any right to engage in any activity or to perform any act aimed at the destruction of any of the rights and freedoms set forth herein.

Nada en esta Declaración podrá interpretarse en el sentido de que confiere derecho alguno al Estado, a un grupo o a una persona, para emprender y desarrollar actividades o realizar actos tendientes a la supresión de cualquiera de los derechos y libertades proclamados en esta Declaración.

Nenio en ĉi tiu Deklaracio estu interpretita kiel implico, ke iu ajn Ŝtato, grupo aŭ persono iel ajn rajtas entrepreni ian ajn agadon aŭ plenumi ian ajn agon, kiu celus detrui kiun ajn el la rajtoj kaj liberecoj ĉi-ene difinitaj.

Keine Bestimmung dieser Erklärung darf dahin ausgelegt werden, dass sie für einen Staat, eine Gruppe oder eine Person irgendein Recht begründet, eine Tätigkeit auszuüben oder eine Handlung zu begehen, welche die Beseitigung der in dieser Erklärung verkündeten Rechte und Freiheiten zum Ziel hat.

Aucune disposition de la présente Déclaration ne peut être interprétée comme impliquant pour un État, un groupement ou un individu un droit quelconque de se livrer à une activité ou d’accomplir un acte visant à la destruction des droits et libertés qui y sont énoncés.

Ничто в настоящей Декларации не может быть истолковано, как предоставление какому-либо государству, группе лиц или отдельным лицам права заниматься какой-либо деятельностью или совершать действия, направленные к уничтожению прав и свобод, изложенных в настоящей Декларации.
本宣言的任何条文,不得解释为默许任何国家、集团或个人有权进行任何旨在破坏本宣言所载的任何权利和自由的活动或行为。

Nenhuma disposição da presente Declaração pode ser interpretada como o reconhecimento a qualquer Estado, grupo ou pessoa, do direito de exercer qualquer atividade ou praticar qualquer ato destinado à destruição de quaisquer dos direitos e liberdades aqui estabelecidos.

Mesi tiga, 2021
Mi xidu na eskri yon ordinari lexi ji jandan jumle.
I try to write using ordinary words and simple sentences.
Denpul eskri sen maxmo asan na doxo, ji folki banto sen maxmo asan na doxo, doxoyen maxmo amiku intreaksyon ton to.
That kind of writing is easier to read, and the easier something is to read, the more deeply readers will engage with it.
Folki ete min yongu energi kos yusu eskrili estilo, ete xa hare max restado to tas yusu idey.
The less energy they expend on your prose, the more they'll have left for your ideas.
Ji ete xa maxmo lungo doxo.
And the further they'll read.
Energi de maxori doxoyen filya na daifucu xafe na doxo bage of makale or esey.
Most readers' energy tends to flag part way through an article or essay.
Eger doxoli motsu sen kufimo xosu, max te duregi finfe fini.
If the friction of reading is low enough, more keep going till the end.
Hay Italili yam hu ren namegi da saltimbocca, hu da mena “tyao cel in munte”.
There's an Italian dish called saltimbocca, which means "leap into the mouth."
Misu cele denwatu hu mi eskri abil na name saltintesta: idey tyao cel in yusu kapi ji yu eskaso xorjui lexi hu da le plasi oto denloka.
My goal when writing might be called saltintesta: the ideas leap into your head and you barely notice the words that got them there.
To sen godo na onxala ki he banwatu eskri ger abil na sen solli idey.
It's too much to hope that writing could ever be pure ideas.
Ible, yu no hata vole dento.
You might not even want it to be.
Mas tas maxori eskriyen, fe maxori mara, dento sen cele.
But for most writers, most of the time, that's the goal to aim for.
Kungan intre maxori eskri ji solli idey no bepulgi poemaya.
The gap between most writing and pure ideas is not filled with poetry.
Maxpul, na eskri jandan sen maxmo lutufpul.
Plus it's more considerate to write simply.
Denwatu hu yu eskri fe dekorapul maner cel na inxo insan, yu kosa ki ete maxpul ergo sol celki yu abil na kwasisen estilopul.
When you write in a fancy way to impress people, you're making them do extra work just so you can seem cool.
To sen sim fe na pospel lungo fustanli koda fe yusu ruke hu yusu doxoyen musi na porta da.
It's like trailing a long train behind you that readers have to carry.
Ji am memori, eger yu eskri in Englisa, ki multi te of yusu doxoyen xa no sen aselli Englisayen.
And remember, if you're writing in English, that a lot of your readers won't be native English speakers.
Ible, etesu aham fe idey sen maxmo suprali kom etesu aham in Englisa.
Their understanding of ideas may be way ahead of their understanding of English.
Fe folo, yu no abil na jadin ki na eskri tem katina tema mena ki yu abil na yongu katina lexi.
So you can't assume that writing about a difficult topic means you can use difficult words.
Mimbay, dekorapul eskri no sol sangu idey.
Of course, fancy writing doesn't just conceal ideas.
Pia, to abil na sangu otosu poshay.
It can also conceal the lack of them.
Denseba ban insan denpul dueskri, cel na sangu fato ki ete hare nilto na loga.
That's why some people write that way, to conceal the fact that they have nothing to say.
Fe kompara, na jandan eskri sengi yu durepulmo cipenkal.
Whereas writing simply keeps you honest.
Eger yu loga nilto jandan, to xa sen mimbay tas moyte, fe inkludi tas yu.
If you say nothing simply, it will be obvious to everyone, including you.
Jandan eskri pia maxmo bon dudure.
Simple writing also lasts better.
Insan hu da xa doxo yusu xey fe xaya xa sen fe banmo sama halu kom insan of alo dexa hu da doxo to nundin.
People reading your stuff in the future will be in much the same position as people from other countries reading it today.
Kultura ji basa xa le alocu.
The culture and the language will have changed.
Yu no sen burfahuri eger dento sen muhim tas yu, samamaner hu to no sen burfahuri, ki moksayyen kostrui kursi cel na dure.
It's not vain to care about that, any more than it's vain for a woodworker to build a chair to last.
Sipul, dudure no sen sol xigoli sifa de kursi, or de eskri.
Indeed, lasting is not merely an accidental quality of chairs, or writing.
To sen ixara ki yu le ergo bon.
It's a sign you did a good job.
Mas fe hataya ki moy hinto sen real fayda of na eskri jandan, nilto of oto sen seba hu mi fale to.
But although these are all real advantages of writing simply, none of them are why I do it.
Cuyo seba hu mi dueskri jandan sen ki na nenjandan eskri cufam mi.
The main reason I write simply is that it offends me not to.
Denwatu hu mi eskri jumle hu da kwasisen godomo fukuza, or hu da yongu hajakalmo eskolyapul lexi, to no kwasisen dekorapul tas mi.
When I write a sentence that seems too complicated, or that uses unnecessarily intellectual words, it doesn't seem fancy to me.
To kwasisen maharakal.
It seems clumsy.
Mimbay, hay mara hu denwatu yu vole na yongu fukuza jumle or dekorapul lexi cel efeto.
There are of course times when you want to use a complicated sentence or fancy word for effect.
Mas yu ingay na nilwatu fale to nyatukal.
But you should never do it by accident.
Alo seba hu misu eskri fe fini sen jandan sen to hu denmaner mi fale to.
The other reason my writing ends up being simple is the way I do it.
Mi velosi eskri unyum xoreskrixey, ji xafe to, mi yongu plu din na penci to, fe na xidu na kosa ki moyto am sen precisomo sahi.
I write the first draft fast, then spend days editing it, trying to get everything just right.
Multi to of hin penci sen na awjeti, ji dento kosa ki jandan eskri sencu hata maxmo jandan.
Much of this editing is cutting, and that makes simple writing even simpler.
Kete le fale to?
Who did it?

tu.note: _I don't know who took it_ would be **Mi no jixi ku kete le cudu to**.

tuv.seg: Bante le cudu to. Mi no jixi ku kete.
Someone took it. I don't know who.
Keto le okur?
What happened?
Mi le fale ban bur to.
I did something bad.
Mi le fale bur banto.
I did something bad.
Hinto sen keto?
What is this?
Hin xey sen lil/day.
This thing is small/big.
Ete sen bon insan.
They are good people.
Multi insan no jixi hinto.
Many people don't know this.
(Fe) duli mara, bur xey okur tas (bon) insan.
Sometimes bad things happen to (good) people.
Jismu de manixu no sen denpul kom jismu de femixu.
The body of a man is not like the body of a woman.
Mida sen mon de insan su jismu. To sen fe inya de jismu.
The stomach is part of people's bodies, it is inside the body.
Hin xey hare dua mon.
This thing has two parts.
Jismu de insan hare multi mon.
People's bodies have many parts.
Hay dua/multi tipo fe nyame.
There are two/many kinds of yam.
Te okocu denpul/sim kom sama tipo (fe mahi). Mas te no sen. Te sen alo tipo.
It looks like the same kind (of fish). But it's not. It's another kind.
Hay (sol) un tipo fe mahi in hin hosu.
There is (only) one kind of fish in this lake.
Hinto sen bon/bur.
This is good/bad.
Hinto sen day/lil basketo.
This is a big/small basket.
Mi le oko hin dua insan; hin moy insan.
I saw these two people; all these people.
Mi le oko sama insan (fe) jaxali din.
I saw the same person the day after.
To le okur in sama loka (fe sama watu), no in alo loka (fe alo watu).
It happened at the same place/time, not at another place/time.
To le okur samaloka/samawatu, no aloloka/alowatu.
It happened at the same place/time, not at another place/time.
Te le fale/loga sama to.
She did/said the same (thing).
Alote le fale to.
Someone else did it.
Te hare kenumer bete?
How many children does she have?
Te hare un bete.
She has one child.
Hay kekwanti sui (in pyale)?
How much water is there (in the bowl)?
Hay multi (xosu, daymo xosu) sui hinloka.
There is much (little, very little) water here.
Multi insan ogar hinloka.
Many people live here.
Le hay multi insan denloka. Xafe dento, dua te le awidi.
There were many people there. After that, two (of them) left.
Bannumer to of hin limon sen bon, bannumer to sen fasidu.
Some of these lemons are good, some are rotten.
In ban plu loka, hay multi kargux.
In some places there are lots of rabbits.
Hay sui hinloka.
There is water here.
Daymo xosu insan ogar denloka hinwatu (or: fe nunya).
Very few people live there now.
Multi te of ete le idi cel dongu, bannumer te le idi cel garebi.
Many of them went to the east, some went to the west.
Tesu moy (man)bete nun sen gamido.
All his sons are now married.
Moy tesu (man)bete nun sen gamido.
All his sons are now married.
Atex le atex moyto in isula.
The fire burned everything in the island.
Bon insan no fale hinpul xey.
Good people don't do things like this.
Hinto le sen bon/bur tas mi.
This was good/bad for me.
To sen bon/bur, eger bante fale ban hinpul to (or: hinpul banto).
It is good/bad if someone does something like this.
Mi bon kone hin person/dom.
I know this person/place well.
Ban insan abil na bon fale hinto, banete no abil.
Some people can do this well, some can't.
Yu fikir tem keto?
What are you thinking about?
Mi le fikir tem to dur lungo watu.
I thought about it for a long time.
Hin person fikir ban bur to tem mi.
This person thinks something bad about me.
Mi le fikir hinmaner:
I thought like this:
Am bon fikir tem to unyum, (leki yu fale to).
Think well about it first (before you do it).
Te sen keloka fe nunya? Mi no jixi. Ible, Mary jixi.
Where is he now? I don't know. Maybe Mary knows.
Te jixi multi tem hinpul xey.
He knows a lot about things like this.
Te le awidi jaledin. Mi jixi.
She left yesterday. I know.
Mi vole ki yu (am) fale to.
I want you to do it.
Mi vole ki hinto (am) okur.
I want this to happen.
Denwatu hu yu oko estare fe noce, yu ganjon keto?
When you look at the stars at night, what do you feel?
Denwatu hu mi nigalu banto, mi hisi daymo bur banto in misu gawlu.
When I swallow something, I feel something very bad in my throat.
Denwatu, mi le ganjon/hisi nilto.
At that time (then), I didn't feel anything.
Denwatu, mi le no ganjon/hisi he banto.
At that time (then), I didn't feel anything.
Mi no haji ganjon he ban bur to tas te.
I don't feel anything bad towards him anymore.
Mi le oko piu denloka.
I saw a bird there.
Xafe dento, mi le oko aloto.
After that, I saw something else.
Te le nun lala -- Mi le ore to.
She was singing -- I heard it.

tu.note: Depending on what exactly is meant by "over", we could say wey denloka or teli denloka or ban denloka for "over there".

tuv.seg: Mi ore banto denloka in ganmoku.
I hear something over there in the bushes.
Mi le no abil na ore to.
I couldn't hear it.
Mi le loga, "Hinto sen bon.
This is good," I said.
Te le loga keto?
What did he say?
Te le loga banto tas te, mas te le no ore to.
He said something to her, but she didn't hear it.
Eger mi fale hinto, insan xa ible loga bur xey tem mi.
If I do this, people can say bad things about me.
Te le loga sama to, mas yon alo lexi.
She said the same (thing), but in different words.
In X-(sa), lexi cel "bon" sen _palya_.
In language X, the word for "good" is _palya_.
Eger yu (xa) loga un max lexi,...
If you say one more word,...
Dento no sen sati.
That's not true.
Yu le fale keto jaxali (xafe dento)?
What did you do then (after that)?
Den insan le fale ban bon to tas mi.
Those people did something good for me.
Insan fale keto yon xey kom hinto (kaxoke, ji max to)?
What do people do with things like this (a spoon, etc.)?
Insan fale hinto yon katatul.
People do this with a knife.
Ban bur to le okur tas hin person.
Something bad happened to this person.
(Fe) den momento, banto le okur fe inya de te (or: in tesu inya; or: in tesu seya).
At that moment, something happened inside him.
Ban bur to le okur in den loka.
Something bad happened in that place.
Am oko! Banto harka denloka.
Look! Something is moving is over there.
Am no harka!
Don't move!
Mi le sen daymo fobido. Mi le no abil na harka.
I was very scared. I couldn't move.
Banto le nun pifu misu hanta.
Something was touching my hand.
Am no pifu to! To sen termopul.
Don't touch it! It's hot.
Hay bante in jarden.
There is someone in the garden.
No hay kumi hinloka.
There are no spiders here.
No hay xabahu.
There are no ghosts.
Hay multi tipo fe jozi.
There are many kinds of nuts.
To sen misu to.
It's mine.
To no sen yusu to. To sen misu to.
It's not yours. It's mine.
Mi jixi ki to no sen misu to. Mi vole ki to (am) sen misu to.
I know it's not mine. I want it to be mine.
Per mesa hay keto? (or: Keto sen per mesa?) Mi no abil na oko to.
What is on the table? I can't see it.
Mi vole na sen ton misu matre.
I want to be with my mother.
To le sen telileli (or: To le sen fe teli leya.). Misu patre le sen nini denwatu.
It was a long time ago. My father was a child at that time.
Mi no jixi ku hinto sen keto.
I don't know what this is.
Mi no jixi ku hinte sen kete.
I don't know who this is.
[In hikaye fe teli ledin] Hin insan (le) jiwa dur lungo watu.
[In story of olden days] These people lived for a long time.
Kacupa jiwa dur lungo watu.
Turtles live for a long time.

At that time she was living with her mother.
Mahi jiwa in bahari.
Fish live in the sea.
Moy insan morcu.
All people die.
Hin insan le morcu telileli (or: fe teli leya).
These people died a long time ago.
Yu le fale to kewatu? Mi le fale to denwatu hu moyte somno.
When did you do it? I did it when everyone was asleep.
Mi no jixi ku to le okur kewatu.
I don't know when it happened.
Samawatu, banto le okur tas mi.
At the same time, something happened to me.
Duli mara, mi glu kafe fe soba; duli mara, mi glu cay.
Sometimes I drink coffee in the morning, sometimes I drink tea.
Hin bwaw moywatu bwawsa fe noce.
This dog always barks at night.
Ete ogar in X hinwatu. Ete le ogar in Y jaleli.
They live in X now. They lived in Y before (this).
To le okur lefe dento. To le okur xafe dento.
It happened beforehand/afterwards.
John le xencu lefe/xafe Harry. (...leki/xaki Harry le xencu.)
John was born before/after Harry (was born).
Hinto le okur telileli (or: fe teli leya).
This happened a long time ago.

tu.note: In a sentence such as this, it would be best to use a noun or proper noun instead of **mante**/**femte**. **Mante** and **femte** are really only used if one wishes to emphasize gender.

tuv.seg: Mante le sen denloka sol dur kurto watu, mas femte le sen denloka dur lungo watu.
He was only there for a short time, but she was there for a long time.
Te le fikir tem to dur bankwanti watu.
She thought about it for some time.
To le okur lefe bankwanti watu.
It happened some time ago.

tu.note: **in** = within, in the space of, in a matter of

tuv.seg: To le okur in un momento.
It happened in one moment.
Te nun sen keloka?
Where is he now?
To le no okur hinloka. To le okur aloloka.
It didn't happen here. It happened somewhere else.
Kam to sen teli fe hinloka?
Is it far from here?
Kam Fred le estay (side) ner fe John?
Was Fred standing (sitting) near John?
Baytu sen ner fe nahir.
The house is near the river.
To sen teli supra geo.

Kapi sen supra alo mon de jismu.
The head is above other parts of the body.
Peda sen infra alo mon de jismu.
The feet are below other parts of the body.
John nun estay fe hin comen (de mi).
John is now standing on this side (of me).

Mary was standing on my right-hand side, Sally was on my left-hand side.

Le hay insan estaydo fe moydua comen de dolo.

There is an insect inside this apple.

Don't open it. You don't know what is inside.

Yu wawa keseba? Koski te le darbe mi.
Why are you crying? Because he hit me.
Eger bante fale hinto, daymo bur banto abil na okur tas insan hinloka.
If someone does this, something very bad can happen to people here.
Ible, te xa ata jaxadin; ible, te xa no (ata jaxadin).

Mi no abil na fale to fe nunya; ible, misu sodar abil.
I can't do it now, maybe my brother can.

I can't move my fingers now.
To sen daymo bon/bur/day/lil.

Hin loka sen daymo teli fe hinloka.
This place is very far from here.
Estare sen daymo daymo teli.

Denwatu hu to le okur tas te, te le hisi/ganjon daymo daymo bur banto.

Mi daymo multi vole na fale hinto.

Max (to)! (Nini fe na wawa cel yam)

I don't know much about it. I want to know more.
Mi vole na oko max.
I want to see more.
Te no haji ogar hinloka.
She doesn't live here anymore.
Mi vole un max to.
I want one more.
Hin nini no sen denpul kom alo nini.
This child is not like other children.

tu.note: **Te** for a live plant; otherwise, **to** is fine.

tuv.seg: Hinto sen sim kom kanabis mas te/to no sen kanabis.

Hello, friend(s)!
Weda, uma!

Mahi suyon.
The fish swim(s).

The fish is/are swimming.

I read.

The dog eats cheese.

Myaw no glu cay.

Kam yu suki na oko filme?

I love you.
Yu lubi mi.
You love me.
Kam patre suki na yam salada?

Yes, the father likes to eat salad.
No, patre no suki na yam salada.

Kitabu sen neo.

Filme sen lungo.
The film is long.
Uma sen day ji bala.
The horse is big and strong.
Te sen mahi.
It's a fish.
Te sen bon patre.
He's a good father.
Den piu sen day.
That bird is big.
Dente sen day.
That (one) is big.
Den piu sen day.
The bird is big.
Juni femixu somno.
The young woman is sleeping.
Sodar ore bon musika.
The sibling listens to good music.
Hin lala sen meli.
This song is beautiful.
Yu hare multi bete mas mi hare xosu _te_.
You have many children but I have few (of them).
Yu le yam xosu jubin ji mi le yam multi _to_.
You ate a little (bit of) cheese and I ate a lot (of it).
Uma velosi pawbu.** or **Uma pawbu velosi.
The horse runs fast.
Matre multi lubi bete.** or **Matre lubi bete multi.
The mother loves the child a lot.
Matre lubi multi bete.
The mother loves many children.
Femixu le hox ore musika.
The woman happily listened to the music.
Manixu le no hox ore musika.
The man didn't happily listen to the music.
Myaw xa velosi glu sui.
The cat will quickly drink the water.
Bwaw xa no velosi glu sui.
The dog will not drink the water quickly.
Myaw sen in banyokamer.
The cat is in the bathroom.
Myaw in banyokamer somno.
The cat in the bathroom is sleeping.
Nini le no multi yam.
The kid didn't eat much.
Bwaw yuxi in parke.
The dog plays in the park.
kete?
who?
kete?
which one?
keto?
what?
keto?
which one?
Medisyen yam keto?

Yu xa doxo ke kitabu?
"You will read which/what book?"

The police officer went to the library (in order) to read a book.
Polisiyen le pawbu cel in kitabudom.
The police officer ran into the library.
Den femyen sen medisyen.
That lady is a doctor.
Alimyen idi cel eskol.
The teacher goes to the school.
Polisiyen hare keto?
What does the police officer have?
Myaw sen keloka?

Myaw sen denloka.
The cat is there.

tu.note: Lesson 8 > Prepositional Phrases without Reference to Location

tuv.seg: Myaw somno fe inya.
The cat is sleeping inside.

tu.note: Lesson 8 > Prepositional Phrases without Reference to Location

tuv.seg: Fe inya, myaw somno.
Inside, the cat is sleeping.
Eskol sen keloka?
Where is the school?
Piu sen fe exya.
The bird is outside.
Bwaw de polisiyen sen day.
The police officer's dog is big.
Polisiyen hare max bete kom musikayen.
The police officer has more children than the musician.
Alimyen yam min roti kom medisyen.
The teacher eats less bread than the physician.
Misu gami max doxo kom mi.** or **Misu gami doxo max kom mi.
My spouse reads more than I.
maxmo meli kom...
more beautiful than...
minmo kotor kom...
less dirty than...
Manixu banyo se.

The man is taking a bath.

Do you love yourself?
Bwaw min somno kom myaw.

Hin drevo sen maxmo lao kom den drevo.

Misu doste suyon in bahari.

Misu mama no kari swinimaso.
My mom doesn't buy pork.
Kam yu suki Mexikoli bira?

Piu sen kepul?

Manixu vole kepul pantalun?

To barix.** or **Hay barix.

To taluji.** or **Hay taluji.

the good (one), the bad (one) and the ugly (one)

(satu) oco, duades lima

tu.note: Content Words: Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives and Adverbs > **Ambitransitive Verbs**

tuv.seg: Dwer le buka**(**cu**)**.
The door opened.

tu.note: Content Words: Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives and Adverbs > Adjective/Adverbs

tuv.seg: Hinto sen _bon yam_.
This is a _good meal_.

tu.note: Content Words: Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives and Adverbs > Adjective/Adverbs

tuv.seg: Bebe _bon yam_.
The baby _eats well_.

tu.note: Content Words: Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives and Adverbs > Adjective/Adverbs

tuv.seg: Uma _velosi pawbu_.
The horse _runs fast_.

tu.note: Content Words: Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives and Adverbs > Adjective/Adverbs

tuv.seg: Bebe yam _bon_.
The baby eats _well_.

tu.note: Content Words: Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives and Adverbs > Adjective/Adverbs

tuv.seg: Bwaw glu sui _velosi_.
The dog drinks the water _quickly_.

tu.note: Content Words: Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives and Adverbs > Adjective/Adverbs

tuv.seg: _Velosi_, bwaw glu sui.
_Quickly_, the dog drinks the water.

tu.note: Content Words: Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives and Adverbs > Adjective/Adverbs

tuv.seg: _Unyum_, te le idi cel banko.
_First_, she went to the bank.

tu.note: Content Words: Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives and Adverbs > Sentence-Initial Active Adjectives

tuv.seg: _Doxone,_ nini le xorsomno.
_Reading,_ the kid fell asleep.

tu.note: Content Words: Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives and Adverbs > Sentence-Initial Active Adjectives

tuv.seg: _Fe na doxo,_ nini le xorsomno.
_Reading,_ the kid fell asleep.

tu.note: Content Words: Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives and Adverbs > Sentence-Initial Active Adjectives

tuv.seg: _Dur na doxo,_ nini le xorsomno.
_While reading,_ the kid fell asleep.

tu.note: Content Words: Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives and Adverbs > Sentence-Initial Active Adjectives

tuv.seg: _Dur na doxo sesu preferido kitabu,_ nini le xorsomno.
_While reading his favorite book,_ the kid fell asleep.

tu.note: Content Words: Nouns, Verbs, Adjectives and Adverbs > Sentence-Initial Active Adjectives

tuv.seg: _Durki te le doxo (sesu preferido kitabu),_ nini le xorsomno.
_While he read (his favorite book),_ the kid fell asleep.

tu.note: Function Words: Conjunctions, Prepositions and Function Adverbs > Expressing Possession

tuv.seg: Baytu de Maria sen day.
"House of Mary is big."

tu.note: Function Words: Conjunctions, Prepositions and Function Adverbs > Expressing Possession

tuv.seg: To de Maria sen day.
Mary's is big.

tu.note: Function Words: Conjunctions, Prepositions and Function Adverbs > Expressing Possession

tuv.seg: Maria su baytu sen day.
Mary's house is big.

tu.note: Function Words: Conjunctions, Prepositions and Function Adverbs > Expressing Possession

tuv.seg: Maria su to sen day.
Mary's is big.

tu.note: Pronouns > Third-Person Pronouns at End of Noun Phrases

tuv.seg: Multi _te_ pala sol in Englisa.
Many (_people_) speak only (in) English.

tu.note: Pronouns > Third-Person Pronouns at End of Noun Phrases

tuv.seg: bon _te_, bur _te_ ji colo _te_
the good (_one_), the bad (_one_) and the ugly (_one_)
Hinto bon nasacu.
This (thing) smells good.
Hin bon nasacu... memorigi mi cel misu femgami.
This good smell... reminds me of my wife.
Kenumer te bon lala?
How many (of them) sing well?
Mi le kari dua kilogramo fe risi. Yu le kari kekwanti to?
I bought two kilos of rice. How much did you buy?

tu.note: Correlatives > Declarative Sentences with Interrogative Phrases

tuv.seg: Mi jixi ku fe ke mesi.
I know in what month.

tu.note: Correlatives > Declarative Sentences with Interrogative Phrases

tuv.seg: Te le no loga ku keseba.
She didn't say why.

tu.note: Correlatives > Declarative Sentences with Interrogative Phrases

tuv.seg: Dento sen ku keloka.
That is where.

tu.note: Correlatives > Declarative Sentences with Interrogative Phrases

tuv.seg: Mi jixi ku na idi keloka.
I know where to go.
Mi ergo** _**denloka hu yu ergo**_**.
I work _where you work_.
Mi xa preata** _**denwatu hu yam sen jumbi**_**.** _or_ _**Denwatu hu yam sen jumbi,**_ **mi xa preata.
I will arrive _when the meal is ready_.
Mi xa preata** _**denwatu hu yam sen jumbi**_**.** _or_ _**Denwatu hu yam sen jumbi,**_ **mi xa preata.
_When the meal is ready_, I will arrive.
Mi le no idi cel parti** _**denseba hu yu idi**_**.
I didn't go to the party _for the reason that you went_.
Mi le xuli mobil** _**denmaner hu yu le alim tas mi**_**.
I fixed the car _how/like you taught me_.
Yu** _**daydenmo**_ **bala.
You are _so_ strong.
Yu hare** _**daydenmo**_ **day oko.
You have _such_ big eyes.
Mi le kari tiga yuxitul tas** _**moyun nini**_**.
I bought three toys for _each child_.
Mi le kari tiga yuxitul tas** _**moy nini**_**.
I bought three toys for _all the children_.

tu.note: Verb Forms > Example Sentences with the Present Perfect in English

tuv.seg: Mi no dupul oko te xorfe mesi tiga.
I haven't seen her since March.

tu.note: Verb Forms > Example Sentences with the Present Perfect in English

tuv.seg: Mi dupul kone te dur 30 nyan.
I have known him for 30 years.

tu.note: Verb Forms > Example Sentences with the Present Perfect in English

tuv.seg: Mi dupul sen gadibu.
I have been angry.

tu.note: Verb Forms > Example Sentences with the Present Perfect in English

tuv.seg: Yu dupul sen kepul?
How have you been?

tu.note: Verb Forms > Example Sentences with the Perfect Progressive in English

tuv.seg: Mi dupul yam hin pingo dur un satu.
I have been eating this apple for one hour.

tu.note: Verb Forms > Example Sentences with the Perfect Progressive in English

tuv.seg: Yu dupul fale keto?
What have you been doing?

tu.note: Verb Forms > Example Sentences with the Perfect Progressive in English

tuv.seg: Mi dupul doxo hin kitabu xorfe jaleli sabedin.
I have been reading this book since last week.
Mi ger yam pingo eger mi sen yamkal.
I would eat the apple if I were hungry.
Myaw le no velosi yam piu.
The cat didn't eat the bird quickly.
Piu le no velosi beyam myaw.
The bird wasn't quickly eaten by the cat.
Mi vole bwaw, mas te am no sen godomo day.
I want a dog, but it should/must not be too big.
Mi hare gutonpul denta; mi am idi cel dentamedisyen.
I have a painful tooth; I need to go to the dentist.
Mi vole ki te am safegi sesu kamer.
I want him to clean his room.
Mi peti ki imi am xorata jaldi.
I ask that we arrive early.
Kitabu hu xwexiyen am doxo da no sen daymo lungo.
The book that the pupils are to read is not very long.
Kam yu am sahay mi?
Could you help me?
Kam yu am klosi janela?
Would you (kindly) close the window.
Eger mi xa yam pingo, mi xa no haji sen yamkal.
If I eat the apple (_in the future_), I will no longer be hungry.
Eger te le yam yusu pingo, kam yu xa sen gadibu?
If he ate your apple (_in the past_), will you be angry?
Eger te yam yusu pingo, kam yu gadibucu?
If he eats your apples (_in general_), do you get angry?

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Determiner + Pronoun = Complete Noun Phrase

tuv.seg: _Banete_ ergo velosi ji _banete_ ergo hanman.
_Some_ work quickly and _some_ work slowly.

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Determiner + Pronoun = Complete Noun Phrase

tuv.seg: Ban ergo sen velosi ji ban ergo sen hanman.
Some work is fast and some work is slow.

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Possessive Adj + Pronoun (Possessive Pronoun) = Complete Noun Phrase

tuv.seg: Yusu gami ergo velosi mas _misu_ te ergo hanman.
Your spouse works fast but _mine_ works slow.

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Possessive Adj + Pronoun (Possessive Pronoun) = Complete Noun Phrase

tuv.seg: Misu ergo sen hanman.
My work/job is slow.

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Quantifier + Pronoun = Complete Noun Phrase

tuv.seg: Dua basataytiyen ergo velosi mas _un te_ ergo hanman.
Two translators work quickly but _one_ works slowly.

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Quantifier + Pronoun = Complete Noun Phrase

tuv.seg: Un ergo sen hanman.
One job is slow.

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Adjective + Pronoun = Complete Noun Phrase

tuv.seg: Day manyen ergo velosi mas _lil te_ ergo hanman.
The big man works quickly but the _small one_ works slowly.

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Adjective + Pronoun = Complete Noun Phrase

tuv.seg: Lil ergo sen hanman.
The small job is slow.
Femyen danse _meli_.
The lady dances _beautifully_.
Mi le gibe pesa tas coriyen _volekal_ koski mi le befobi ki te xa morgi mi.
I gave the money to the thief _involuntarily_ because I feared he would kill me.
Manyen _no godomo bur_ danse.
or: **Manyen danse _no godomo bur_.**
Manixu _no danse godomo bur_.
The man _doesn't dance too badly_.

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Adverbs of Focus

tuv.seg: Misu gami glu _sol_ kafe fe soba.
My spouse drinks _only_ coffee in the morning.

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Adverbs of Focus

tuv.seg: Misu gami glu kafe _hata_ fe axam.
My spouse drinks coffee _even_ in the evening.

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Adverbs of Focus

tuv.seg: _Pia_ misu gami glu kafe fe soba.
My spouse, _too_, drinks coffee in the morning.

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Complex Adjective Phrases

tuv.seg: kitabu eskrido fal misu doste
the book written by my friend

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Complex Adjective Phrases

tuv.seg: alimyen hox kos yusu sukses
the teacher happy for your success

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Complex Adjective Phrases

tuv.seg: nini maxmo lao kom misu sodar
the kid older than my brother

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Relative Clauses with Resumptive Pronoun

tuv.seg: Te sen femixu _hu da lubi mi_.
"She is the woman _who that-one loves me_."

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Relative Clauses with Resumptive Pronoun

tuv.seg: Te sen femixu _hu mi lubi da_.
"She is the woman _who I love that-one_."

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Relative Clauses with Resumptive Pronoun

tuv.seg: Mi le sonxi katatul _hu mi kata roti yon da_.
"I lost the knife _which I cut the bread with that-one_."

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Relative Clauses with Resumptive Pronoun

tuv.seg: Kamisa _hu mi suki da_ sen blue.** or **To sen blue, kamisa _hu mi suki da_.
"The shirt _which I like that-one_ is blue." or "It's blue, the shirt _which I like that-one_."

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Relative Clauses with Resumptive Pronoun

tuv.seg: Te sen manixu _hu dasu sodar kone mi_.
"He is the man _who his brother knows me._"

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Relative Clauses with Resumptive Pronoun

tuv.seg: Te sen manixu _hu mi kone dasu sodar_.
"He is the man _who I know his brother_."

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Relative Clauses with Resumptive Pronoun

tuv.seg: Manyen _hu dasu gami Globasa_ sen misu doste.** _or_ **Te sen misu doste, manyen _hu dasu gami Globasa_.
"The guy _who that-one's spouse speaks Globasa_ is my friend."

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Relative Clauses with Resumptive Pronoun

tuv.seg: Manyen _hu dasu gami Globasa_ sen misu doste.** _or_ **Te sen misu doste, manyen _hu dasu gami Globasa_.
"He's my friend, the guy _who that one's spouse speaks Globasa_."

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Relative Clauses with Resumptive Correlative Adverb

tuv.seg: Kitabudom _hu mi ergo denloka_ sen day.
"The library _which I work there_ is big."

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Relative Clauses with Resumptive Correlative Adverb

tuv.seg: Kitabudom _hu denloka mi ergo_ sen day.
"The library _which there I work_ is big."

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Relative Clauses with Resumptive Correlative Adverb

tuv.seg: Din _hu mi xa preata denwatu_ sen Lunadin.
"The day _which I arrive then_ is Monday."

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Relative Clauses with Resumptive Correlative Adverb

tuv.seg: Din _hu denwatu mi xa preata_ sen Lunadin.
"The day _which then I arrive_ is Monday."

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Relative Clauses with Resumptive Correlative Adverb

tuv.seg: Kitabudom _hu mi ergo in da_ sen day.
"The library _which I work in it_ is big."

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Relative Clauses with Resumptive Correlative Adverb

tuv.seg: Kitabudom _hu in da mi ergo_ sen day.
"The library _which in it I work_ is big."

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Relative Clauses with Resumptive Correlative Adverb

tuv.seg: Din _hu mi xa preata fe da_ sen Lunadin.
"The day _which I arrive on it_ is Monday."

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Relative Clauses with Resumptive Correlative Adverb

tuv.seg: Din _hu fe da mi xa preata_ sen Lunadin.
"The day _which on it I arrive_ is Monday."

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Relative Clauses in Non-Specific Noun Phrases

tuv.seg: Mi no suki _to hu mi ergo denloka_.
"I don't like _it which I work there_."

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Relative Clauses in Non-Specific Noun Phrases

tuv.seg: Mi no suki _to hu denloka mi ergo_.
"I don't like _it which there I work_."

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Relative Clauses in Non-Specific Noun Phrases

tuv.seg: Mi suki _to hu yu broxa misu tofa denmaner_.
"I like _it which you brush my hair that way_."

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Relative Clauses in Non-Specific Noun Phrases

tuv.seg: Mi suki _to hu denmaner yu broxa misu tofa_.
"I like _it which that way you brush my hair_."

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Relative Clauses in Non-Specific Noun Phrases

tuv.seg: Am gibe tas mi _to hu mi vole da_.
"Give me _it which I want that_."

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Relative Clauses in Non-Specific Noun Phrases

tuv.seg: Mi no suki _te hu yu le seleti da_.
"I don't like _her/him/them who you chose that-one._"

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Relative Clauses in Non-Specific Noun Phrases

tuv.seg: Mi no suki _loka hu mi ergo in da_.
"I don't like _the place which I work in that_."

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Relative Clauses in Non-Specific Noun Phrases

tuv.seg: Mi no suki _loka hu in da mi ergo_.
"I don't like _the place which in that I work_."

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Relative Clauses in Non-Specific Noun Phrases

tuv.seg: Mi suki _maner hu yu broxa misu tofa yon da_.
"I like _the way which you brush my hair in that_."

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Relative Clauses in Non-Specific Noun Phrases

tuv.seg: Mi suki _maner hu yon da yu broxa misu tofa_.
"I like _the way which in that you brush my hair_."

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Relative Clauses in Non-Specific Noun Phrases

tuv.seg: Am gibe tas mi _xey hu mi vole da_.
"Give me _the thing which I want that_."

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Relative Clauses in Non-Specific Noun Phrases

tuv.seg: Mi no suki _person hu yu le seleti da_.
"I don't like _the person who you chose that-one._"

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Non-relative Modifying Clauses

tuv.seg: Singa begude idey _feki maux ger abil na sahay te_.
The lion was tickled by the idea _that the mouse could help him_.

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Clauses with _feki_ instead of Relative Clauses with _hu_

tuv.seg: Mi no suki _restoran feki imi le yam_.
"I don't like _the restaurant that we ate at_."

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Clauses with _feki_ instead of Relative Clauses with _hu_

tuv.seg: Te sokutu _(fe) moy mara feki te estaycu_.
"He falls every time that he stands up."

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Clauses with _feki_ instead of Relative Clauses with _hu_

tuv.seg: Mi suki _maner feki yu broxa misu tofa_.
"I like _the way that you brush my hair_."

tu.note: Word Order: Phrase Structure > Clauses with _feki_ instead of Relative Clauses with _hu_

tuv.seg: _Seba feki yu no xwexi_ sen koski yu no abyasa.
"The reason that you don't learn is because you don't practice."
Myaw sen keloka?
Where is the cat?
Filme sen kewatu?
When is the movie?
Uma (sen) perfetomo syahe.
The horse is perfectly black.
Mi suki na lala.
I like to sing.
Mi musi na ergo.
I must work.
Mi musi na ergo.
I have to work.
Mi no abil na danse.
I cannot dance.
Gitara sen asan na soti.
The guitar is easy to play.
Mi sen jumbi na idi.
I am ready to go.

tu.note: ​Word Order: Sentence Structure > Nominal Verb Phrases

tuv.seg: Cele sen na triunfa.
The goal is to win.

tu.note: ​Word Order: Sentence Structure > Nominal Verb Phrases

tuv.seg: Na sen nensabar sen problema.
To be impatient is a problem.

tu.note: ​Word Order: Sentence Structure > Nominal Verb Phrases

tuv.seg: To sen problem, na sen nensabar.
It is a problem to be impatient.

tu.note: ​Word Order: Sentence Structure > Nominal Verb Phrases

tuv.seg: Na soti gitara sen asan.
To play the guitar is easy.

tu.note: ​Word Order: Sentence Structure > Nominal Verb Phrases

tuv.seg: Na soti gitara sen asan.
Playing the guitar is easy.

tu.note: ​Word Order: Sentence Structure > Nominal Verb Phrases

tuv.seg: To sen asan, na soti gitara.
It is easy to play the guitar.

tu.note: ​Word Order: Sentence Structure > Nominal Verb Phrases

tuv.seg: Na suyon in bahari sen amusane.
To swim in the sea is fun.

tu.note: ​Word Order: Sentence Structure > Nominal Verb Phrases

tuv.seg: Na suyon in bahari sen amusane.
Swimming in the sea is fun.

tu.note: ​Word Order: Sentence Structure > Nominal Verb Phrases

tuv.seg: To sen amusane, na suyon in bahari.
It is fun to swim in the sea.

tu.note: ​Word Order: Sentence Structure > Nominal Verb Phrases

tuv.seg: Te le sokutu dur na danse.
He fell while dancing.

tu.note: ​Word Order: Sentence Structure > Nominal Verb Phrases

tuv.seg: Fe na doxo, nini le xorsomno.
Reading, the boy fell asleep.

tu.note: ​Word Order: Sentence Structure > Prepositional Phrases

tuv.seg: Myaw _in sanduku_ somno.
The cat _in the box_ is sleeping.

tu.note: ​Word Order: Sentence Structure > Prepositional Phrases

tuv.seg: _In sanduku,_ myaw yam maux.
The cat eats the mouse _in the box_.

tu.note: ​Word Order: Sentence Structure > Prepositional Phrases

tuv.seg: Myaw sen _fe inya._
The cat is _inside_.

tu.note: ​Word Order: Sentence Structure > Prepositional Phrases

tuv.seg: Myaw _fe inya_ somno.
The cat _inside_ is sleeping.

tu.note: ​Word Order: Sentence Structure > Prepositional Phrases

tuv.seg: _Fe inya_, myaw somno.
_Inside_, the cat is sleeping.
Mi gibe kitabu _tas nini_.
I give the book _to the child_.
Mi gibe _tas nini_ kitabu.
I give _the child_ the book.
Mi gibe kitabu _tas te_.
I give the book _to her/him_.
Mi gibe _tas te_ kitabu.
I give _her/him_ the book.
Mi gibe to _tas nini_.
I give it _to the child_.
Mi gibe to _tas te_.
I give it _to her/him_.
_Tas nini_ mi gibe kitabu.
_To the child_ I give a book.
_Tas te_ mi gibe to.
_To her/him_ I give it.
Baytu _fe kapi de_ liljabal sen kimapul.
The houses _on top of_ the hill are expensive.
Baytu _fe kapi_ sen kimapul.
The houses _on top_ are expensive.
_Fe kapi_, baytu sen kimapul.
_On top_, the houses are expensive.
Kimapul baytu sen _fe kapi_.
The expensive houses are _on top_.

tu.note: ​Word Order: Sentence Structure > Prepositional Verbs

tuv.seg: Myaw inya.
The cat is inside.

tu.note: ​Word Order: Sentence Structure > Prepositional Verbs

tuv.seg: Myaw ruke sanduku.
The cat is behind the box.

tu.note: ​Word Order: Sentence Structure > Prepositional Verbs

tuv.seg: Myaw ruke.
The cat is in the back.
Hay multi kitabu in kitabudom.
There are many books in the library.
Hay barix.** or **To barix.
"There is rain." or "It rains."
Hay termo.** or **To sen termopul.
"There is heat." or "It is warm."

tu.note: ​Word Order: Sentence Structure > Clause in Place of Subject

tuv.seg: To no surprisa mi, ki yu le xuli mobil.

Yu ogar keloka: in Barati or Indonesi?
"You live where: in India or Indonesia?"

tu.note: Common Phrases and Expressions > Common Questions/Replies

tu.note: Common Phrases and Expressions > Common Questions/Replies

tu.note: Common Phrases and Expressions > Common Questions/Replies

so-so

tu.note: Common Phrases and Expressions > Common Questions/Replies

tuv.seg: Mi name...** _or_ **Misu name sen...

tu.note: Common Phrases and Expressions > Common Questions/Replies

tu.note: Common Phrases and Expressions > Common Questions/Replies

tu.note: Common Phrases and Expressions > Common Questions/Replies

Yu dupul fale keto?
What have you been doing?
Mi dupul doxo hin kitabu xorfe jaleli sabedin.
I have been reading this book since last week.
Mi ger yam pingo eger mi sen yamkal.
I would eat the apple if I were hungry.
Myaw le no velosi yam piu.
The cat didn't eat the bird quickly.
Piu le no velosi beyam myaw.
The bird wasn't quickly eaten by the cat.
Mi vole ki te am safegi sesu kamer.
I want him to clean his room.
Mi peti ki imi am xorata jaldi.
I ask that we arrive early.

tu.note: [Singularity vs plurality and the overuse of plu: ban as a case study] Consider the sentence-initial use of ban din (some day or some days) in the following example sentences. Notice how if we want to say "some days" we can still just say ban din without the need to introduce plu since the verb form (with or without du-, or present vs past/future) would indicate whether we're speaking about a general habit (plural) or a one-time occurrence.

tuv.seg: Ban din, mi jagecu dyer.
Some days I wake up late. (present tense: habitual)

tu.note: [Singularity vs plurality and the overuse of plu: ban as a case study] Notice how if we want to say "some days" we can still just say ban din without the need to introduce plu since the verb form (with or without du-, or present vs past/future) would indicate whether we're speaking about a general habit (plural) or a one-time occurrence. Some days I wake up late. (present tense: habitual)

tuv.seg: Ban din, mi le dujagecu dyer.
Some days, I would wake up late.

tu.note: [Singularity vs plurality and the overuse of plu: ban as a case study] Some days I wake up late. (present tense: habitual) Some days, I would wake up late. (du-: habitual)

tuv.seg: Ban din, mi xa loga tas te satiya.
Some day (or One day), I will tell him the truth.

tu.note: [Singularity vs plurality and the overuse of plu: ban as a case study] Some days, I would wake up late. (du-: habitual) Some day (or One day), I will tell him the truth.

tuv.seg: Ban din, mi le loga tas te satiya.
One day, I told him the truth.

tu.note: [Singularity vs plurality and the overuse of plu: ban as a case study] On the other hand, it has occurred to me that it would be useful for the numeral un to be used as a determiner to mean "a certain". This is in contrast to ban, which is ambiguous and can be either singular or plural. Using un in place of ban to mark singularity doesn't add an extra word, making its systematic use less awkward than the repetitive use of plu to mark plurality would, since plu adds a word rather than replaces. So the last two example sentences above could also be expressed using un din instead of ban din:

tuv.seg: Un din, mi xa loga tas te satiya.
Some day (or One day), I will tell him the truth

tu.note: [Singularity vs plurality and the overuse of plu: ban as a case study] So the last two example sentences above could also be expressed using un din instead of ban din: Some day (or One day), I will tell him the truth

tuv.seg: Un din, mi le loga tas te satiya.
One day, I told him the truth.

tu.note: [yamgi vs yamgibe] Now, the problem with the direct object of yamgi potentially working either way is that if there's only one argument, we should probably assume it's the recipient (Mi le yamgi myaw), but what if it's not? What if we actually intend for it to be the patient? In that case, using yamgibe would work best to avoid confusion (Mi le yamgibe maux). If we really wanted to express a more forceful causation, depending on the context and intended meaning (degree of agency or intentionality), we could use verbs like musigi, pel, lide (?) (and others).

tuv.seg: Opera pel te na wawa.
Opera makes her cry. ("Opera drives her to tears.")

tu.note: [yamgi vs yamgibe] If we really wanted to express a more forceful causation, depending on the context and intended meaning (degree of agency or intentionality), we could use verbs like musigi, pel, lide (?) (and others). Opera makes her cry. ("Opera drives her to tears.")

tuv.seg: Lalayen pel te na wawa.
The singer makes her cry.

tu.note: [yamgi vs yamgibe] The singer makes her cry. The boss makes her cry.

tuv.seg: Filmekef musigi atoyen na wawa.
The director had the actress cry. (obliged her to cry)

tu.note: [sangu (hide) to be recategorized as transitive; atex (burn) and teslimu (surrender) to remain ambitransitive] sesangu - intr: hide (oneself) By the way, remember that in practice se- verbs typically function transitively with the reflexive direct object pronoun:

tuv.seg: Mi le sangu se.
I hid (myself).

tu.note: [Various meanings of "for": cel, tas, fol, fe] The preposition fol means "according to". It can be translated as "for", but only in this sense ("according to one's opinion or view"). For me, this is the most beautiful animal.

tuv.seg: Fol mi, hinto sen maxmo meli hewan.

Now notice how the meaning of "for" in the following sentences is different from those described above: "This medicine works for humans", "This is good for you", "For children, the risk is great", "For me, 40 degrees is too warm" ("For me" as in how it affects my body personally, rather than as an opinion in general).

tu.note: [Grammar addition: Colon Questions] ### Colon Questions Colon questions in Globasa are as follows.

tuv.seg: Yu suki keto: kafe or cay?
"You like what: coffee or tea?"

tu.note: [Grammar addition: Colon Questions] "You like what: coffee or tea?" Do you like coffee or tea?

tuv.seg: Yu ogar keloka: in Barati or Indonesi?
"You live where: in India or Indonesia?"

tu.note: [Revised "Omission of Verb Particles"] If I eat the apple (in the future), I will no longer be hungry.

tuv.seg: Eger te le yam yusu pingo, kam yu xa is gadibu?
If he ate your apple (in the past), will you be angry?

tu.note: [Grammar Addition: Continuative Aspect (dupul)] Globasa's compound tenses include the following perfect (completed) tenses. Present Completed: nun le

tuv.seg: Mi nun le yam pingo.
I have eaten the apple.

tu.note: [Grammar Addition: Continuative Aspect (dupul)] I have eaten the apple. Past Completed: le le

tuv.seg: Mi le le yam pingo.
I had eaten the apple.

tu.note: [Grammar Addition: Continuative Aspect (dupul)] I had eaten the apple. Future Completed: xa le

tuv.seg: Mi xa le yam pingo.
I will have eaten the apple.

tu.note: [Grammar Addition: Continuative Aspect (dupul)] "I have always guided him" The adverb dupul is also used with stative verbs (verbal and adjectival):

tuv.seg: Mi dupul kone te dur 30 nyan.
I have known him for 30 years.

tu.note: [basa vs loga vs eskri and the names of languages as verbs] By the way, the preposition fe should logically be used here. (I think I have "loga Globasa" in the website, so this would actually be an adjustment.)

tuv.seg: Mi loga fe Espanisa.
Mi speak (in) Spanish.

tu.note: [Prefix proposal: nen-] We currently use the word no as a prefix meaning un- (and all other variations). Whereas this is fine with adjectives, in the case of verbs (including stative) verbs, there's a slight ambiguity that can arise, if not in writing at least in speech:

tuv.seg: Mi no kox.
I am not happy.

tu.note: [The Infinitive in Globasa] * Verb Complements I like to sing.

tuv.seg: Mi musi na ergo.
I must work. *or* I have to work.

tu.note: [The Infinitive in Globasa] I like to sing. I must work. or I have to work.

tuv.seg: Mi no abil na danse.
I cannot dance.

tu.note: [The Infinitive in Globasa] I must work. or I have to work. I cannot dance.

tuv.seg: Gitara asan na soti.
The guitar is easy to play.

tu.note: [The Infinitive in Globasa] I cannot dance. The guitar is easy to play.

tuv.seg: Mi jumbi na idi.
I am ready to go. ​

tu.note: [The Infinitive in Globasa] With copula is* sentences as shown above: In these sentences, the infinitive verb phrase may be moved to the end of the sentence if it is not already in that position.

tuv.seg: Cele is na triunfa.
The goal is to win.

tu.note: [The Infinitive in Globasa] The goal is to win. To be impatient is a problem.

tuv.seg: Is problem na sabarkal.
It is a problem to be impatient.

tu.note: [The Infinitive in Globasa] To play the guitar is easy. or Playing the guitar is easy.

tuv.seg: Asan na soti gitara.
It is easy to play the guitar.

tu.note: [The Infinitive in Globasa] To play the guitar is easy. or Playing the guitar is easy. It is easy to play the guitar.

tuv.seg: Na suyon in bahari amusane.
To swim in the sea is fun. *or* Swimming in the sea is fun.

tu.note: [The Infinitive in Globasa] It is easy to play the guitar. To swim in the sea is fun. or Swimming in the sea is fun.

tuv.seg: Amusane na suyon in bahari.
It is fun to swim in the sea.

tu.note: [The Infinitive in Globasa] * As the complement of a preposition: fe tayday de na danse - Instead of dancing

tuv.seg: Te le sokutu dur na danse.
He fell while dancing.

tu.note: [The Infinitive in Globasa] fe tayday de na danse - Instead of dancing He fell while dancing.

tuv.seg: Fe na doxo, nini le xorsomno.
Reading, the boy fell asleep.

tu.note: [The Infinitive in Globasa] The last portion (as the complement of a preposition) is a slight adjustment. Previously, the infinitive was not used after a preposition. This, however, creates an ambiguity.

tuv.seg: Te le sokutu dur danse.
He fell during the dance. (not necessarily while he was dancing)

tu.note: [The Infinitive in Globasa] He fell during the dance. (not necessarily while he was dancing) He fell while dancing. (while he was dancing)

tuv.seg: Fe doxo, nini le xorsomno.
At the reading, the boy fell asleep. (the boy wasn't necessarily the reader)

tu.note: [Grammar Adjustment Proposal: iji... ji; oro... or...; noro... nor....] nor... nor... - neither.... nor... The idea is borrowed from Esperanto, and although in works well in Esperanto, it doesn't work as well in Globasa due to nouns and verbs having the same form. For example, in direct object position ji (both) can easily be interpreted to mean "and" even after the object has been uttered.

tuv.seg: Mi estudi ji danse ji lala.
I study both dance and song, or I study and dance and sing.

tu.note: [Suiwol Kraw (First original story in Globasa)] but the water was at the bottom. It thought for some time.

tuv.seg: Te preporta bannumer lilpetra ji
It brought some pebbles and

tu.note: [Suiwol Kraw (First original story in Globasa)] It thought for some time. It brought some pebbles and

tuv.seg: plasi oto fe inya de kaxa.
placed them in the container.

tu.note: [Suiwol Kraw (First original story in Globasa)] The water came up. It drank the water.

tuv.seg: Kox, te awfley.

tu.note: [Updated ke vs ku- correlatives section] You might notice the different ways of saying "like/as". You are like me.

tuv.seg: Kupul mi, pia te ergo in kitabudom.
Like me, she too works at the library.

tu.note: [Updated ke vs ku- correlatives section] Mi salom yu kuli misu sodar. (I had "kupul" previously, but I think "kuli" makes more sense here.) I greet you as my brother.

tuv.seg: Kumaner mi le loga...
Like I said...

tu.note: [Grammar Adjustment: ke- vs. ku- correlatives] Formerly, ke- correlatives were used only in direct questions other than kam (yes/no) questions. ku- correlatives were used only in statements. In spite of being a simple division of labor for ke- and ku- correlatives, this does not appear to work well in practice. For example, the following sentence is ambiguous, just as it is in English (although English differentiates by whether or not who is stressed):

tuv.seg: Mi le swal tas misu tie kute suki cokolateli keke.
I asked my uncle who likes chocolate cake.

tu.note: [Grammar Adjustment Proposal: extending use of "-su" as genitive particle for all nouns] Currently, the suffix -su is used as a possessive adjective marker applied to pronouns. It seems inevitable that -su would end up being experimentally used for nouns as well. I suggest we make -su official for this use, but apply it as a separate word, rather than a suffix. As a separate word, proper nouns would remain intact in form as well as in pronunciation of stress.

tuv.seg: Maria su baytu kijawi. = Baytu de Maria kijawi.
Mary's house is green.

tu.note: [Today, yesterday and tomorrow] Currently the words for today (nundina), yesterday (leja dina or ledina) and tomorrow (xaja dina or xadina) can be used as either nouns or adverbs.

tuv.seg: Mi le yuxi pedabol ledina.
I played soccer yesterday.

tu.note: [Today, yesterday and tomorrow] Currently the words for today (nundina), yesterday (leja dina or ledina) and tomorrow (xaja dina or xadina) can be used as either nouns or adverbs. I played soccer yesterday.

tuv.seg: Ledina le is bono dina.
Yesterday was a good day.

tu.note: [Today, yesterday and tomorrow] I played soccer yesterday. This would parallel sentences such as the following:

tuv.seg: Mi le yuxi pedabol fe dina dua.
I played soccer on Tuesday.

tu.note: [Today, yesterday and tomorrow] This would parallel sentences such as the following: I played soccer on Tuesday.

tuv.seg: Te xa preata fe dina lima.
He will arrive (on) Friday.
